about: Turn rules that OpenStreetMap does not carry, with their source. Applied to the network by 07_turn_rules.py (run from 02_build_net.sh). OpenStreetMap turn restriction relations and turn:lanes arrows are read by netconvert itself; 07_turn_rules.py checks that each restriction inside the network was applied. 'ban' deletes a turn. 'hook_turn' keeps the right turn but makes it from the kerb (leftmost) lane, as a Melbourne hook turn is: the driver keeps left, waits in the hook-turn box, and turns when the cross street gets green. The box itself is not modelled (see README, Turn rules). Directions are compass directions of travel.

rules.source: DTP Traffic Signal Configuration Data Sheet DOC/24/198884 (12/08/2024): no car right-turn signal group from La Trobe St westbound into Swanston St, only a bike hook turn. OpenStreetMap has no restriction here.
rules.note: Not yet checked on site. This is the turn the shortcut through the closed block needs. Skip it with 07_turn_rules.py --allow 2921-latrobe-westbound-right-ban for the sensitivity case.

rules.source: DTP sheet, operation spec 1/07/2024: two hook-turn boxes inside the junction (detectors 13 and 14). La Trobe St has centre tram tracks, so its right turns are hook turns. Russell St has no trams.

DTP sheet, plan 555670C rev B (19/07/2024): three hook-turn boxes (detectors 11, 12 and 19). Both streets have tram tracks. OpenStreetMap's turn:lanes tags (left;right|through) already make the Elizabeth St right turns hook turns, and restriction relation 9348872 bans one La Trobe St right turn, which leaves one La Trobe St hook turn: three boxes in all, as on the sheet.

no_sheet_turn_info.about: Junctions with a detector sheet read (detector_approaches.json) whose turn signals were not read. Their turn rules come from OpenStreetMap only.
